notes.title: Patch 1.20 - BIG UI Overhaul, QoL Improvements!
notes.notes:
Big UI & QoL Update + Localization improvements



Localization
Corrected the descriptions text of some talent nodes for Blancara The Ice Dragon, wrongfully some nodes showed the chinese description in the japanese localization.

The mini-games/quick time events were missing the translations for the "hit the space" bar information - this has now been added and also been increased in size a bit for readability
UI / QoL
The map, collection and bestiary is now split into different interfaces providing more clarity and readability and making things easier to navigate especially for new players.

The navigation bar on the left can now be toggled off so players can take in the whole map if they want. 

Commissions inside the navigation bar can now be clicked and will open the pre-battle modifier window as if you would select the respective raid separately. It will also immediately adjust the modifiers so that you have a chance to encounter the enemies necessary in order to complete the commission.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/a6acc87c945a9f30d4b881185ff638402f7e7fa7.jpg"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/ffa27eaccfd36dedfa50d0e4531da083564b92a9.jpg"]

All info boards from the location, raids and commissions have been visually updated and matching the color of the races/regions they belong to. Instead of auto showing the quite big infoboards on hover and covering a lot of the map, they have now been reduced to the small info icon on the right end of the banners. The commission infoboards in particular have received a substantial visual update showing now not only the commission descriptions but also a snippet of the required map region, the required modifiers (night, boss etc.) as well as a rarity info for those who are not 100% encountered each raid. Plus another art to indicate the target.

The squad swapping has been made more clear. If you hover your current squad in the collection scene you will immediately notice a clear swap icon indicating the option to swap. Furthermore all current selected members will be listed as the first 4 cards in the collection making it more clear. Also there are now arrow indicators at the top and bottom of the card selection indicating if there is still room to scroll so players don't miss potential characters hidden at the bottom of the scroll view.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/12c946640841f10f91c645fd65a50aedc67f0d3b.jpg"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/209502e421a1aca34d38f3ef0d7fa5b2306c67b5.jpg"]

The archivum is basically a bestiary and has therefore been renamed and although sometimes finding your own terms for your fantasy world can be nice - in some cases it does not hurt to stick with what is known for simplicity. The bestiary has also received some visual improvements making such as race fitting color indicators on the preview page as well as some ornaments.

The end turn icon has multiple times been criticized, rightfully so, so there is a new one which makes it more clear that it is about moving on to the next character.

Also a big but important info often lost, is the fact that armor only protects against ranged attacks. I'm aware that the tutorial in battle includes a lot of information and therefore small things can get lost. I highlighted this info more to make it more clear. However in the future I plan on adding additional tooltips or pop ups when it happens so players get reminded. (remind me on that one haha)

During battle the bestiary and the action menu (right click) can be escaped via clicking anywhere outside - however I still added a close icon and info to avoid confusion.

The info pop ups in the Action Menu (right click) for the Wait Option, End Turn Option, abilities (1-3) and basic attacks have been visually changed making it more distinct and clear. The abilities are blue as the potential target frames, the basic attack is red also like the frame of potential targets. Also the ability info pop ups from the player hud at the bottom have been changed to blue to make sure new players associate blue frames on enemies with potential targets for the selected ability.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/9a6cf720c5704fb0946f098e39d9f46c8914fbd2.jpg"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/8168728e52336652630d3cd8ee5dba90eeb82b30.jpg"]

The location interface of Wokasa has also received some visual updates such as new headline banners with ornaments fitting the Tagari, and as well as info boards and banners fitting the respective race in the hiring window. Furthermore the scouting and recruiting now have a confirmation pop up to avoid instant buys as well as an info that players should consider to keep coins to heal and repair. The commissions from Wokasa are active from beginning, this has also led to some confusion for this current build - in the final version this won't be an issue since they can be actually taken but for now I made it clear that these are already active.

The menu and raid start buttons with holding option have now a lower holding time to speed things up.

Sometimes players decided to skip the tutorial in the management scene (map, collection etc.) before or after the battle - This should now be prevented but if it is still done the tutorial will not pop up again it will be marked as completed. However the bonus of renown will not be given to the player.

Speaking of tutorial, some task descriptions, input markers etc. have been improved and simplified hopefully leading to less confusion.

The starting coin amount has been increased from 200 to 300 making it a bit easier to heal & repair early on until players get the grip of the game.

I think that's it, I hope you like the new art background of the collection and the bestiary in the management scene.




Lastly - For those interested in the future of the project.
My Kickstarter will go live on Sep 16th. So in less than 10 days. It will feature low tiers including the complete game with Early Access and some Kickstarter exclusives for a bit less than 13 usd. For those interested to support the project even more or secure real collectibles, the campaign will feature printed! - yes printed cards (like trading cards) as well as a short comic and lore-art book. For mega enthusiasts, if you want to create your own character or boss, this will be possible too. With the funding I hope to bring the vision of Fangs & Forges to life.

Check out Kickstarter



If you want to learn more about myself, the history of the project and detailed future plans you can check out this interview I gave IGD (Indie Game Developer) recently.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/38d7bad97f534c7420bea41c4f3d170efc85aeca.jpg"]

Check out Interview





And please make sure to

Wishlist if you haven't

follow on Steam

leave a demo review (super helpful!)

and follow the Kickstarter so you don't miss the Early Bird specials



Thank you for reading and your passionate interest in the project,

Alpenwolf

notes.notes:
Localization Update
Besides English, the demo is now available in:

German 🇩🇪

French 🇫🇷

Spanish 🇪🇸

Polish 🇵🇱

Russian 🇷🇺

Japanese 🇯🇵

Chinese Simplified 🇨🇳



If your system is set to one of these languages, it should set the language accordingly; otherwise, it will remain in English. You can manually change the language in the settings menu.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/80e98278813ea4c5b396f92a547bbade785d75f9.png"]

Some parts of certain languages have been improved by community members. However, the translations are certainly not perfect, so please don’t take any offense in that and let me know if you find anything. I’ll try to fix it asap. Overall, I hope for all non-English speakers that this is still an improvement. In the future, for official releases and such, you can expect professional translations for sure.


Remaining Patch Notes (QoL changes)
Right Click Squad Member "Circle Portraits" in collection window for details

Right Click Hex Cards on the battlefield to open the character's "Archivum" page

If characters are equipped with Consumables, they now pop up at the beginning of the turn on the left side as a reminder so they can be used - as they must - before any actions.

I updated the tips which can be set active in the battlefield scene

I also added more tooltips & improved some wording


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/829b178086759c2360bccf2c79c6f335d54bd308.jpg"]
Future Plans
I hope to be soon ready for more updates on release plans etc. For now the Kickstarter release is planned for around the end of September. The additional funds will help to add more battlefields, enemy mobs, item art, campaign mode, and story trailer.

My plan is to hold a permanent closed beta after the campaign until the Early Access launch with regular patches, which will steadily introduce new characters, battles, or mechanics to test and provide feedback.

The current goal is to release into Early Access around April/Mai 2026. I'm also in talks with potential publishers, maybe there will be some updates in this regard too. 

If you like to support the project & grab yourself some fancy printed cards, make sure to follow the Kickstarter and get notified: LINK

Have a nice weekend,
Alpenwolf

notes.title: Patch 1.11 - NEW Champion, Real-Time Events, Buffs/Nerfs & More
notes.notes:
New Character "Kapu Novani Chas'awi"
The highlight of this patch is a new playable character! He’s part of the starting roster—no unlocking required!

Open the demo, swap him in, and let’s go!

To keep this short, here’s his Archivum description:
A Macawi bruiser, unyielding and fierce. His mammoth skull shield deflects blows, while his whip lashes with versatile fury, bone armor and tusk marking his indomitable might.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/170ce44bc4349e73f72eae6d9d6173b4c682689b.jpg"]
Remaining Patch Notes
Besides a few small bug fixes (mostly text), I've made some stat changes. To experience them, you’ll need to reset your progress (if you want)

Valash & Kishk: Initiative reduced by 1. Still higher than the common Naphas but toned down to better align with other races like the Tagari.

Bandit Boss (Turtle): Armor lowered from 100 to 50. He’s already beefy with high physical resistance and life points. Now, a ranged, kiting squad can take him down more effectively.

Juvo, the Assassin: Big multiplier boost to Rain of Daggers and increased Atk Skill. As a vulnerable hybrid (not a full marksman with total battle range), he needs to get up close in fights. This change makes that risk more rewarding.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/29a5daf3a61919e73f28e712e5efd761ea289c98.jpg"]
Real-Time Events.
As mentioned in early Dev Logs, I wanted to add mini-games and real-time events to some characters. So far, the demo only had one example since its March release (Juvo’s “Headshot” ability). The success of Expedition 33 recently showed this can be a great feature for turn-based games.

In F&F, with 100+ characters, this mechanic is an optional spice for players who enjoy it—not mandatory. With the new character Kapu, I leaned into this. His lore and design fit perfectly, so I crafted the Whip Hook ability. Kapu uses his whip to pull an enemy to the nearest free hex next to him. Nail the real-time event for bonus damage; hit the bright green area for perfect timing, and you’ll stun the target. It’s not too easy, so costing only 1 ability charge feels like a solid reward. We’ll see how it plays out! :)

Strategically, the goal is to pull a target closer to your squad or away from an ally. A stun is the cherry on top. I’m pumped to hear your thoughts—especially after you try it! I’d love to add more of these if they’re balanced, not too punishing, and suit the character’s design. Drop your feedback!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/e0cb5d2e4240ddb7774b1a3643d953967851e7d9.jpg"]
Upcoming localization
The next patch will add new languages to the demo. Planned sooner or later:

French 🇫🇷

German 🇩🇪

Japanese 🇯🇵

Russian 🇷🇺

Spanish 🇪🇸

Others? Let me know in the comments.


Printed Cards? New Battlefields? More Enemies?
Want more battlefields, cities to explore, or enemies and bosses to defeat? Sign up on the Kickstarter Pre-launch page!

The KS campaign will include a Closed Beta tier, updating from the demo to Early Access release, accessible via Steam for backers. If beta testing isn’t your thing, maybe grab printed cards, an exclusive comic, or an art-lore book.

Some perks are limited or only available in the first hours/days, so sign up to get notified! 


👉 Kickstarter Pre-Launch Page


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/8a53d7af97a948e678fa320450475642b094f0f9.jpg"]Pages from Short Comic taking place in Firnend -  featuring several characters of the Nordur.

notes.title: Patch 1.10 - First Major Update
notes.notes:
Intro
Hey everyone, Patch 1.10 is finally here! It took longer than planned—my computer crashed, and digging through backups was a nightmare. But it’s done, and I’m thrilled to share it. Your feedback these past weeks has been incredible - some of you poured serious time into detailed notes, and I’ve addressed ~90% of your suggestions, if not more. The support and positive reviews for Fangs & Forges keep me going, so thank you. Let’s get to it!

Quick Note
As a solo dev, I’ve made countless small tweaks I didn’t fully track. Writing exhaustive patch notes at this stage takes time away from development, so I’m keeping things high-level for now. Please let me know if you’d prefer super-detailed notes going forward or if this format works!

Core Features in Patch 1.10 (From 1.01 to 1.10)  

 Ranks (Meta Leveling): You, the commander, now rank up through renown earned from defeating enemies and completing quests. 
 The Archivum: A medieval bestiary-style journal to track enemy stats, abilities, and resistances. Unlock details by fighting them, viewable in battle (“character detail”) or on the map scene. 
 Tutorial Overhaul: Completely reworked for clarity and flow—excited to hear your thoughts.
 Tooltip Clarity: Added tooltips, larger text, and improved visuals for better readability.  
 UI Overhaul: Smoother, more intuitive, and more legible (bigger text where needed), based on your feedback.  
 New Battle Input System: Select abilities or basic attacks directly from the battle HUD bar.  
 Simplified Battle HUD: Cleaner, less cluttered, but fully functional.  
 Level-Up Info Window: Post-battle screen details which stats improved and by how much.  
 Steam Demo Achievements: Fun challenges like finishing the tutorial, defeating bosses, or reaching rank milestones.
 Battle Experience System: Units gain a +1% bonus to a special stat (e.g., Block Chance, Fire Resistance) on level-up, based on defeated enemies’ traits. Details below!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/853ae3b19b627123b077753ffb0ebe39d6662f73.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/4137597ded506d79db0d8c1ca27b1d4ae0fbbc21.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/d822120ed20a2bd0318be03fccd9f67bd3213537.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/10b50c892f2e475cc2ed973a6b3e5a9ae06c0c0b.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/39d4d7deba4379218266a51322d7ef7594df01d7.jpg

Minor QoL & Tweaks

 Battle Adjustments: Minor balancing changes (not the focus yet).  
 Ability Damage Scaling: Tied to base damage and multipliers for clarity, as requested.
 Heal/Repair All Button: One-click squad recovery.  
 Visible Stats: Top-corner preview shows enemy stats if you’ve scouted them enough.


Bug Fixes

 Fixed inventory not loading in the Map Scene.  
 Retaliation kills now award XP.  
 Speed potions function correctly.  
 Madness Potion applies its speed buff properly.  
 Plus other minor fixes.


Join Us
Want to discuss leveling, mechanics, or Fangs & Forges? Join our Discord:
DISCORD SERVER

Future Plans  

 Day/night mechanics (e.g., weaker ranged attacks at night).  
 Squad "loadouts" for quick team setups.  
 More mini-games/quick-time events for abilities, blocking, or grievous wounds (like the Headshot ability).  
 Quick-breakaway & retaliation rework: Adjacent units get frequent breakaway strikes (not counting as retaliation), keeping the 1-retaliation-per-round limit.


Deep Dive: Key Topics
1) Balancing Info vs. Immersion
Your feedback about unclear unit stats hit home—there wasn’t enough info to make informed choices beyond gut instinct, which frustrated some of you. I’ve added tooltips, the Archivum, and visible stats to give you the tools to strategize, but I’m careful not to overdo it. My philosophy for Fangs & Forges is fast, immersive skirmishes where you learn enemy patterns through experience, not by leaning on UI crutches or crunching numbers.

For example, the core damage mechanic—Attack Skill vs. Defense Skill—adjusts damage by 10% per point difference. It’s simple to grasp: if your unit’s Attack Skill is 5 and the enemy’s Defense Skill is 3, you deal +20% damage. Secondary factors like range penalties or movement bonuses (e.g., ranged attacks before moving) are minor, letting experienced players squeeze out extra efficiency without bogging down newbies. The Archivum now reveals resistances (e.g., high Fire Resistance explains low damage), helping you adapt without spoon-feeding every detail

I tested features like toggles for exact HP, armor, or predicted damage but scrapped them—they cluttered the HUD and broke the "in-the-moment feel" of battle. I want you to focus on tactical decisions—positioning, timing, and unit matchups—not math. My goal is to keep battles face-paced and distinct from slower, hyper-tactical games. With the Archivum and cleaner UI, I think we’re hitting the sweet spot—enough info to plan, but not so much it feels like “AFK fighting.” What do you think?  

2) Level-Ups & Battle Experience

How Level-Ups Work  
Core Stats: Attack Skill, Defense Skill, Damage, Initiation, and Base Attack Efficiency increment subtly each level (e.g., +0.1 Attack Skill per level, +3 total by level 30) Stats update at whole numbers (e.g., 5.9 stays 5; 6.0 becomes 6).  

Why Subtle?: Keeps stats tight (1-10 range, except Damage at 10-80) for clear, strategic duels, inspired by Heroes of Might and Magic 3. A 1-point Attack vs. Defense gap = +10% damage, easy to calculate. Speed is skill-tree-only due to its impact.  

Skill Tree: Nodes at levels 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 allow boosts like +1 Attack Skill or +1 Speed, shaping your unit’s role.  

Items: Rare items (e.g., +3 Attack Skill) match 30 levels of growth, with expanded stats planned.  

Why This Design?
With a large roster, I avoid stat-point micromanagement to preserve each unit’s unique identity. Low stat ranges ensure distinct matchups (e.g., high Attack Skill units counter high-defense tanks; high Damage units excel vs. equal-defense foes). Skill trees and items offer customization without homogenizing units. This design also places significant weight on loot and gear, as rare items provide powerful stat boosts that rival extensive leveling, enhancing strategic customization.

Battle Experience (New!)
Units gain a +1% bonus to a special stat (e.g., Block Chance, Fire Resistance) on level-up, based on the enemies they defeat:

 Enemies have a Primary Trait (e.g., +2% Block Chance)
 and Secondary Trait (e.g., +1% Fire Resistance).  


Defeating enemies accumulates these bonuses (e.g., 3 enemies = +6% Block Chance, +3% Fire Resistance). On level-up, the highest accumulated stat gets +1% (capped at +10% per stat). If capped, the next highest non-capped stat is chosen.  

Example: Kill 3 enemies (Primary: +2% Block Chance, Secondary: +1% Fire Resistance). Pool: +6% Block Chance, +3% Fire Resistance. Level-up gives +1% Block Chance. If capped, +1% Fire Resistance applies.  

Strategy: Fight specific enemies to tailor units (e.g., blockers for Block Chance, fire enemies for Fire Resistance). Secondary traits ensure progress even if a stat is capped.

This system adds depth, letting your battles shape unit growth without complex management.

Wrap-Up
Please note that all previous progress will be reset upon starting this version due to significant changes in character leveling and stat mechanics.

Please also note that these features and mechanics are subject to change, so feel free to share your feedback. 

Looking ahead, expect news about the release date and new content (characters, raids, etc.) soon. I’ve focused on refining the demo and core features to a high standard before moving to the next phase. Thank you for your understanding and support!

Patch 1.10 is a major step forward, and I’m eager for your feedback. Join our Discord or leave a review—your input shapes this game. Let’s keep building Fangs & Forges together!

notes.title: Demo Patch 1.01 – First Update & Fixes
notes.notes:
Alrighty, time for the first patch! This update primarily focuses on bug fixes, QoL improvements, and addressing some of the most common feedback from players. Let’s jump right in!

🔥 Major Hotfix – Freeze After First Battle
Some players experienced the game freezing after completing the first battle tutorial. This happened if all tutorial steps (Move, Attack, Use Ability, etc.) weren’t followed exactly, leaving the tutorial incomplete.

To fix this, the tutorial is now automatically marked as completed once the first battle ends, regardless of whether all steps were manually triggered. This should eliminate the issue entirely.

If you ran into this bug make sure to use Reset in the main menu and resetting the tutorial in settings. If any issues persist, let me know! 

🐛 Bug Fixes
 Frozen units from Blancara’s Frost Breath can no longer block or retaliate (obviously, haha).
 Equipment that provides armor couldn’t be unequipped if it was damaged or depleted. Now, you’ll get a clear tooltip error message informing you that repairs are needed before unequipping. Previously, only the error sound played.
 Jupo’s Madness Potion could be thrown on empty hexes—this is now fixed.
 Soratros’ Spinning Attack ability description incorrectly stated that it could damage allied units, but that was never the case. The description has been corrected.

🛠 Quality of Life Improvements
Easier Character Navigation
 You can now navigate between character details using arrows instead of having to close and reopen different characters.
 This works in both the Collection and the Squad menu on the map screen, keeping the current tab (Abilities, Items, etc.) open as you switch.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/7d37d201ef61c4a67c91a4ee94828e9cbc1f2d1c.png

Reset Confirmation & Settings Improvements
 Resetting your progress in the main menu now requires confirmation, preventing accidental resets.
 Volume settings now have separate sliders for Music and SFX.
 Resetting the tutorial now shows a tooltip, confirming that it worked.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/3a6081672cf9000b5b82006f6b6fddf48d15f1d2.png

📌 Other Notes
Some players reported that Jupo’s Madness Potion wasn’t increasing movement properly. I tested it, and it worked fine for me. Keep in mind: The effect lasts for 3 turns, so if you throw the potion at someone and they don’t act until 4 turns later, the effect will have already expired. I’ll keep an eye on this one!

🔜 Next Patch (Planned for the Weekend)
This was a small update, but I’m already working on the next patch, which will include:
✔ Better display of stats, effects, and abilities for enemies & characters during battle
✔ Option to heal/repair armor for all characters in the collection
✔ More detailed ability damage info
✔ Access to base formulas—how damage, effects, and stats are calculated
✔ Post-battle level-up window with detailed information
✔ More bug fixes & general polish.

Thanks for all the amazing feedback so far! Keep it coming, and I’ll continue improving things 💪🔥

Let me know if I forgot something.

notes.title: Demo Release Announcement
notes.notes:
The Fangs & Forges Demo will release on March 21st. 

Step into a world of tactical combat, squad management, and high-fantasy battles in Fangs & Forges. In this almost feature-complete demo, you’ll explore challenging battlefields, recruit unique characters, complete commissions, and test your strategies against deadly foes. Whether you're pushing through waves of enemies or facing down formidable mini-bosses, every encounter brings an opportunity to refine your tactics and uncover powerful loot.

Master Tactical Combat with Precision & Strategy
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/2a18ea6102acfb5a657336b682057ce6dbff1e7b.jpg
In F&F, battles are won through smart ability usage, precise positioning, and perfect timing. Every ability counts - Whether you’re stunning enemies into battlefield edges, blocking movement with burning fields, or chaining abilities together for devastating effects, mastering these elements is the key to victory.
 Leverage Unique Abilities – Every character has distinct skills that can interact or synergize with each other for maximum impact.

 Adapt to Different Fighting Styles – Build a squad with a mix of melee, hybrid, and ranged fighters, utilizing roles like bruisers, assassins, skirmishers, and tanks.

 Inflict & Avoid Deadly Combat Statuses – Effects like grievous wounds, poison, frozen, stunned, or feared can control the battlefield—but enemies can use them against you too.

 Enhance Your Squad with Equipment – Gear up with weapons and armor to boost damage, defense, and survivability, while also modifying special stats such as block chance, life steal, and armor penetration.

 Survive Mini-Boss Fights & Enemy Waves – Stock up on consumables like life potions and ability recharges to endure prolonged battles.

 Customize Character Progression – Unlock skill tree nodes to upgrade base stats such as attack skill, defense skill, and more.

What Awaits You in the Demo?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/b0634a21f3281f2c381ecbd0e3332faa17152799.jpg
 9 Playable Squad Members – Start with 7 characters and recruit 2 more using renown and coins earned in battle.

 2 Raid Locations – Each location features day & night variants, mini-boss encounters, and scalable difficulty through enemy waves, increasing loot quality and coin rewards.

 Character Progression – Level up your squad to level 5, unlocking their first skill points for customization within their skill trees.

 Loot & Equipment – Earn randomized gear and consumables across different rarity tiers to enhance your team’s effectiveness.

 Complete 2 Quests – Take on additional challenges and earn valuable rewards.
A Glimpse Into the Full Game
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45034631/71c00ebee00c8d2092c54a8b1ff4953f2bd3482b.jpg
The demo offers just a taste of what’s to come. The full version of Fangs & Forges will expand upon this foundation with:

 Over 100 more recruitable characters from 4 unique races, each with unique abilities, fully designed artwork, and rich backstories.

 Dozens of new battlefields, featuring varied enemy types, mini-bosses, and challenging layouts.

 A deep skill tree system, with characters leveling up to 30, unlocking six powerful upgrades.

 A living world, where the map evolves over time, as corruption spreads across regions, altering available locations and encounters.

 A fully fleshed-out item system, featuring custom artwork and diverse equipment to enhance your squad.

Almost Feature-Complete & Highly Replayable
This demo is not just a small preview—it’s a polished, meaningful slice of the final game. While only a fraction of the full experience, it already delivers a nearly feature-complete battle system and core gameplay loop.

For those who have followed the project for a while, the demo release has been long in the making. Initially planned much earlier, I ultimately decided that a great demo is a crucial tool. Instead of rushing it, I kept iterating—adding more mechanics, refining combat, and implementing deeper features than originally expected. A lot of behind-the-scenes playtesting also went into ensuring a balanced and engaging experience, which added to the delay but made for a much stronger result.

The demo offers at least an hour of fun for players who enjoy experimenting—try out different squad compositions, hunt for powerful loot, and take on the challenging bosses. But even for those just giving it a quick spin, playing for 20 minutes already provides a solid glimpse into the game’s vision, mechanics, and whether it's something they’d enjoy. In any case, it’s worth a try!
